Class Telemetry

java.lang.Object
frc.spectrumLib.telemetry.Telemetry
public class Telemetry extends Object
Telemetry and logging facade, backed by AdvantageKit.

In 2026 this class extended DogLog. On SystemCore it keeps the same static API (log, logDash, logDashAlways, print, time/timeEnd, slowLogThisLoop), so every existing call site compiles unchanged. Every value is now an AdvantageKit output (Logger.recordOutput(String, byte[])). Outputs land in the same wpilog as the replayed inputs, under /RealOutputs/... on the robot and /ReplayOutputs/... in replay, so a replayed match regenerates every one of these keys from the code under test.

Rules that come with AdvantageKit

  • Main thread only. Logger is not thread-safe. Nothing on a Notifier, the CTRE odometry thread or a vision callback may call this class; hand the data to the main loop and log it there (see Swerve's odometry queue).
  • Outputs never drive logic. Anything a decision depends on must come from a logged input (Logger.processInputs(String, LoggableInputs)), or replay will diverge.

Tiers

  • log(String, double) records to the log only.
  • logDash(String, double) / logDashAlways(String, double) record to the log and mark the key as a dashboard key, which DashboardReceiver also sends to NetworkTables. Only dashboard keys (these, and every key the Elastic layout reads) go to NT, unless the "/SmartDashboard/Telemetry/MirrorLogsToNT" switch is on. That is the 2026 offseason rule, for the CPU it costs.
  • slowLogThisLoop() is true at 10 Hz whatever the loop rate. Wrap logs that do not need loop-rate resolution (currents, temperatures, vision status) in it.

    • time

      public static void time(String key)
      Starts a timed span. Pair with timeEnd(String) on the same key.

      Uses the real clock, not Logger.getTimestamp(), because the point is to measure how long the code took. In replay these values describe the replay machine, not the robot.

      Parameters:
      key - the log key the elapsed time will be written to

    • timeEnd

      public static void timeEnd(String key)
      Ends a timed span and logs its length in seconds, so existing analysis of the Scheduler/* keys keeps working.
      Parameters:
      key - the key passed to time(String)

    • logEvent

      public static void logEvent(String key, String message)
      Logs a discrete event. AdvantageKit keeps one value per key per cycle. Logging two messages to the same key in one loop kept only the second, so two commands ending in the same loop, or two prints, lost one. Events are accumulated per loop and recorded as a string array holding all of them.
      Parameters:
      key - the log key
      message - the event
